source.title: LLM-Virus: Evolutionary Jailbreak Attack on Large Language Models
source.authors: Miao Yu; Jun-Feng Fang; Ying-Jie Zhou; Xing Fan; Kun Wang; Shirui Pan; Qing-Song Wen

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or wrong-document issue. Some tables are flattened in the supplied text, so their individual numeric entries cannot be assigned confidently.
record.tranche_reason: The paper develops and evaluates an evolutionary jailbreak attack, relying on the general premise that jailbreaks can bypass safety mechanisms. It does not test fine-tuning effects, token-position KL, compliant-opening prefills, or the stated mechanism of shallow safety.
record.gate_note: The paper reports outcomes for its own jailbreak method and some transfer attacks. These are recorded under fits_no_version: they do not isolate any of the claim versions. Baseline comparisons and ablations of the paper's attack method are not separately recorded as claim results. Table II and Table III entries are omitted where the flattened layout does not support reliable attribution.
record.test_reason: The paper builds and evaluates an evolutionary jailbreak-template attack (LLM-Virus) and reports its own method's attack success against baselines. It does no fine-tuning, per-token KL, prefilling or decoding manipulation, parameter localization, or deepening training. Jailbreak templates wrap the query rather than forcing a compliant opening, so V4 is not isolated either.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that LLM-Virus performs comparably or better than several baselines across safety benchmarks, with good transferability and lower time cost. Ablations support its design choices.
record.recipe_differences: This paper evolves jailbreak templates using LLM-based crossover, mutation, and fitness evaluation. It does not reproduce either original source's fine-tuning intervention or token-depth/KL analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported attack outcomes vary with host model and template source. The local-evolution experiment also reports dependence on generation temperature and evolutionary components, but those ablations concern the attack method rather than the claim's proposed safety mechanism.

fits_no_version.finding: Evolved jailbreak templates raise LLM-judged attack success on GPT-4o, Claude-3.5 and GPT-3.5-Turbo. Transfer across hosts varies: it fails on Claude-3.5-Haiku and is strong from GPT-4o-mini templates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Black-box evolutionary jailbreak templates raise harmful compliance in safety-aligned LLMs, with host-dependent transferability.

record.problems: For the claim at issue, the experiments do not test fine-tuning, token-position effects, prefilling, or parameter localization. The reported safety-related outcomes are jailbreak attack-success measurements, not tests of the proposed shallow-safety mechanism. The text says LLM-Virus results are averaged over three runs, but gives no uncertainty estimates. Some supplied table entries are flattened and cannot be attributed reliably.
record.rows_left_out: Table II and Table III contain flattened attack-success-rate values whose model/method/metric assignments are not sufficiently clear in the supplied text; no values from those tables are included. Ablation results in Section V.D compare components of the authors' attack method rather than testing the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No per-token KL or position analysis.

No prefilling of a compliant start, adversarial-suffix study of response openings, or decoding change. Only prompt-template jailbreaks are tested. GCG baselines are cited and compared as competing methods, not as tests of V4.
No analysis of the data or training objective as causes.

record.verdict_notes: This is an attack-method paper. All rows are the authors' own method performance and none bear on any version. Tables II and III are baseline comparisons of attack methods and are rightly excluded. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or resulting refusal/compliance measurement.
No fine-tuning on benign data or resulting refusal/compliance measurement.
No per-token KL or aligned-versus-base distribution measurement.
Does not isolate compliant-opening prefills, suffixes, or decoding changes as ways of getting past initial response tokens. It evaluates a distinct evolutionary jailbreak-template method.
No weight, rank, or parameter localization experiment.
No test of whether data or training objectives produce shallow safety.
No training to deepen safety or evaluation of whether such training holds up.
